introduction_markdown: GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, General Certificate of Education Examination. 0796 INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGIES 1, ADVANCED LEVEL, JUNE 2021. Multiple choice question paper. Duration: one and a half hours. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination. All questions carry equal marks. Electronic calculators are not allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Decide which answer is correct, find the number of the question on the answer sheet and draw a horizontal line across the letter to join the square brackets for the answer you have chosen. Mark only one answer for each question (if more than one answer is marked, the question scores zero). Avoid spending too much time on any one question. Do all rough work in the booklet.
incertitudes: Page de garde vérifiée : GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, JUNE 2021, ADVANCED LEVEL, 0796 INFORMATION AND COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGIES 1, QCM de 50 questions de même valeur, durée une heure et demie ; les calculatrices et les téléphones sont interdits. Aucun point n'est imprimé. Le sujet ne compte que 4 pages (page de garde et 3 pages de questions) et ne contient aucun code C ou Pascal, aucun SQL, aucune figure : rien n'a été compilé ni exécuté dans un SGBD.

Sujet scanné (CamScanner, filigranes gcerevision.com ignorés), sans corrigé officiel : toutes les clés sont déduites et les corrigés rédigés. Les calculs de Q10 (addition binaire 77 + 56 = 133), Q17 (345 en binaire) et Q30 (8 To / 8 Go) ont été recalculés par script Python.

Défauts d'impression du sujet : coquilles dans les énoncés (« Nano Hetz » en Q6, « Winmax » pour WiMAX en Q49, « eFAT » en Q46, « Pre-relational dependency » en Q45), recopiées telles quelles ; les options C et D de Q14 (« Full duplex » et « Duplex ») désignent la même chose.
Q6 : le sujet impose le mégahertz, seule unité réaliste parmi les quatre options ; les processeurs de téléphone actuels s'expriment en gigahertz (clé retenue C).

Clés retenues en QCM avec une marge de doute (questions « devinettes » ou options proches) : Q4 (pilote plutôt que changement par étapes), Q12 (prototypage, dont l'affinement pas à pas est la définition ; RAD défendable), Q20 (TPS pour des vendeurs, MIS défendable), Q27 (la localisation, alors que l'URL indique aussi le protocole), Q35 (les dépendances entre tâches, alors que le coût n'apparaît pas non plus dans un diagramme de Gantt) et Q44 (commutateur ; le point d'accès est défendable).

Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 9, 13, 14, 31, 42, 46. Q9 : les options C et D (« at a time » et « in that system ») disent la même chose ; Q13 : le code-barres ne porte qu'un numéro, ni B (prix) ni D (nom) n'est exact ; Q14 : les options C et D (full duplex, duplex) sont équivalentes ; Q31 : toutes les options sont associées à l'enseignement en ligne selon les plateformes ; Q42 : la caméra web et le téléphone sont également non indispensables ; Q46 : NTFS et exFAT (probablement visé par « eFAT ») sont tous deux des systèmes de fichiers 64 bits. Réponse visée dans chaque corrigé.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following components of the computer can be used as both input and output device?
questions.corrige_markdown:
An input device only sends data into the computer (keyboard), an output device only receives results from it (VDU, printer). A digital versatile disk (DVD) is a storage medium: its drive can **read** data from it (input) and, for a recordable or rewritable disk, **write** data to it (output). It is the only component in the list that works in both directions.

The keyboard is input only; the visual display unit and the laser printer are output only. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT true about databases?
questions.corrige_markdown: A database is built to give several users shared access to the same data (information sharing), to protect it (security) and to keep it accurate and consistent (integrity). Its great advantage over separate files is that it **reduces** data redundancy, because each fact is stored once. Saying that a database *increases* redundancy is therefore false. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a project management technique?
questions.corrige_markdown: PERT charts, Gantt charts and the Critical Path Method (CPM) are used to plan, schedule and monitor the tasks of a project. SDLC (System Development Life Cycle) is not a scheduling technique: it is the sequence of phases (investigation, analysis, design, implementation, maintenance) followed when developing a system. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: If the implementation of a new system is tried out only in a part of the organisation, it is described as:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a **pilot** implementation the new system is installed and tested in only one part of the organisation (one branch, one department) before it is extended to the rest. Parallel running keeps the old and the new system working side by side everywhere. Phased and piecemeal changeovers replace the old system progressively, stage by stage or module by module, across the organisation, and are not a trial in one location. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Optical storage devices employ:
questions.corrige_markdown: CDs, DVDs and Blu-ray disks store data as pits and lands on a reflective track. The drive reads (and writes) them with a **laser beam**. Electromagnetic fields are used by magnetic storage (hard disks, tapes). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The speed of the processor of an android phone is measured in terms of :
questions.corrige_markdown: Processor speed is the clock frequency, in hertz. Nano and pico are fractions of a hertz (far too slow to be a clock) and kilohertz is the order of magnitude of the first microprocessors' clocks of the 1970s. Of the four options only the **megahertz** is a realistic unit for a phone processor (today's phones actually quote gigahertz, 1 GHz = 1000 MHz, which is the same family of unit). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Encryption and decryption provides confidentiality but NOT:
questions.corrige_markdown: Encryption scrambles data so that only the holder of the key can read it: this gives confidentiality and privacy, and, combined with digital signatures and checksums, authentication and integrity. A **patent right** is a legal protection of an invention; no cryptographic technique grants it. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transmission mode between a radio transmitter and a receiver is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A radio (or television) broadcast station only transmits and the receiver only receives: data flows in **one direction only**. That is simplex transmission. Asynchronous and synchronous describe how bits are timed, not the direction of flow, and full duplex would need both ends to send at the same time (as on a telephone). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following best describes mono tasking operating system?

*Options as printed:* A) The operating system is designed for a particular program   B) Only one user is allowed to use the system   C) Only one program can run at a time   D) Only one program can run in that system
questions.corrige_markdown:
A mono-tasking (single-tasking) operating system runs **one program** and does not start a second one until the first has finished (MS-DOS is the classic example). Option B describes a single-user system, which is a different property: a single-user system can still be multitasking. Options C and D are close in wording; D ("only one program can run in that system") is the closest to the definition, while C ("at a time") describes the same idea, so the printed wording is ambiguous.

**Intended answer: D (Only one program can run in that system).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The result of the arithmetic operation 1001101 +111000 in binary is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Convert and add: $1001101_2 = 77$ and $111000_2 = 56$, so the sum is $77 + 56 = 133 = 10000101_2$ ($128 + 4 + 1$).

Binary column addition gives the same result:

```
  1001101
+ 0111000
---------
 10000101
```

The other options are $197$, $229$ and $245$ in decimal. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The information system that does NOT generate any organised information is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A decision support system (DSS), a management information system (MIS) and an executive information system (EIS) all process data into summaries, reports and models that managers use. A **transaction processing system (TPS)** only records the day-to-day transactions (sales, payments, orders); it captures raw data and produces no analysed or summarised information on its own. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A stepwise refinement approach in system development is used in:
questions.corrige_markdown: In **prototyping**, a first working model is built from the basic requirements, shown to the users and improved again and again, each pass refining the previous one, until the users accept it. The waterfall method moves once through the phases without going back, and outsourcing is about who does the work, not how. Rapid application development also uses prototypes, but the step-by-step refinement of a prototype is the defining feature of prototyping. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
One major benefit of using barcode is

*Options as printed:* A) It provides detailed information on all key aspects of the product   B) It provides the selling price of the product   C) It provides the identity of the shop   D) It provides the name of the product
questions.corrige_markdown:
A barcode is a pattern of bars that encodes a product number. When the reader scans it, the till looks the number up in a database to **identify the product** (name, and then the price). The bars hold only the number, not the detailed information (option A) and not the shop (option C). Between B (price) and D (name) the printed options are not precise, since both come from the database lookup; the identity of the product is the benefit that is closest to the definition.

**Intended answer: D (It provides the name of the product).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The interactive transmission of data within a time sharing system may be best suited by:

*Options as printed:* A) Simplex lines   B) Half duplex lines   C) Full duplex lines   D) Duplex lines
questions.corrige_markdown:
A time-sharing system serves many users at terminals who type a request and receive the answer, so data has to flow in both directions; a **full duplex** line carries both directions at the same time, which is what an interactive session needs. Simplex is one way only. Half duplex works in both directions but one at a time. The difficulty with the printed options is that C ("full duplex") and D ("duplex") mean the same thing, so the question has two equivalent answers.

**Intended answer: C (Full duplex lines).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A code written by a programmer is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: The program text that a programmer writes in a high-level language is the **source code**. The compiler translates it into object (machine) code. "Syntax code" and "instruction code" are not standard terms. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cash dispenser which can also give a report of the current balance in a customer's account is an example of:
questions.corrige_markdown: An automatic teller machine reads the customer's account at the moment of the request and answers immediately, with the account updated as soon as the withdrawal is made: this is **real time (online transaction) processing**. Batch processing collects transactions and processes them later, all at once. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Convert the decimal number 345 to binary.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Successive division by 2 (remainders read from the bottom up):

$345 = 2 \times 172 + 1$, $172 = 2 \times 86 + 0$, $86 = 2 \times 43 + 0$, $43 = 2 \times 21 + 1$, $21 = 2 \times 10 + 1$, $10 = 2 \times 5 + 0$, $5 = 2 \times 2 + 1$, $2 = 2 \times 1 + 0$, $1 = 2 \times 0 + 1$.

Reading upwards: $101011001_2$. Check: $256 + 64 + 16 + 8 + 1 = 345$. The other options are $371$, $341$ and $397$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following registers carries the address of the next instruction to be executed by CPU?
questions.corrige_markdown: The **program counter** (instruction pointer) holds the address in memory of the next instruction; it is incremented at each fetch. The instruction register holds the instruction currently being decoded, and the accumulator holds the data and the results of arithmetic. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The importance of a query in a DBMS is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A query asks the database a question: it selects the records (and fields) that satisfy a criterion, from one table or from several. Editing and entering data are the jobs of forms, and combining tables permanently is not what a query does (a query only presents a joined result). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Extract specific information stored in one or more tables based on a given criterion.
Provide user friendly interface to edit information on tables
Provide interface to enter information to specific records
Link information from several tables into one

questions.enonce_markdown: A suitable information system for sales persons is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Sales persons work at the operational level: they record orders, invoices and payments, which is the job of a **transaction processing system (TPS)**. An EIS serves senior executives, a GIS handles geographical data and an MIS produces summary reports for middle managers (an MIS could also be defended, since sales reports come from it, but the persons who make the sales use the TPS). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A tool used in SDLC to model a new system from a logical point of view is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **data flow diagram** shows what data enters the system, which processes transform it, where it is stored and where it goes, without saying how it is physically implemented: it is a logical model. A flowchart details the steps of an algorithm or procedure, a PERT chart schedules a project and simulation tests behaviour. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a step used in software development by prototyping?
questions.corrige_markdown: Prototyping starts by identifying the **basic requirements** (the main inputs and outputs), then builds a first model, lets the users try it and refines it. Fact-finding about the old system and a logical appraisal belong to the analysis phase of the traditional life cycle, and buying hardware comes at implementation. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Collection of data about the old system

questions.enonce_markdown: A precise report generated by an MIS to call for the attention of an unusual event to alert managers is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: An **exception report** is produced only when something falls outside the normal limits (stock below the minimum, expenses above budget) to draw the manager's attention to it. A periodic report is issued at regular intervals, a demand report on request, and a summary report condenses large amounts of data. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The performance of a computer is mostly determined by:
questions.corrige_markdown: The performance of a computer depends mainly on how fast the CPU executes instructions (clock speed, number of cores) and how much RAM it has to hold the programs and data in use. The operating system is software with no "speed" of its own, and the BIOS is small and has little effect. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The speed of the operating system and memory size
The speed and the number of input/output it can handle
The processor speed and memory size
The size of the BIOS and memory size

questions.enonce_markdown: The general form of the IF statement is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The selection statement has the general form `IF <condition> THEN <statement>` (with an optional `ELSE` part). `DO ... UNTIL` is a repetition (loop) structure. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The system development model that does NOT allow overlapping of phases is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: In the **waterfall model** each phase must be finished and signed off before the next one starts, with no overlap and no return. The spiral and iterative models repeat phases in cycles, and the V model pairs each development phase with a testing phase, which overlaps in practice. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A URL is the full address for an Internet resource. What does it specify?
questions.corrige_markdown: A Uniform Resource Locator, for example `http://www.example.com/page.html`, gives the protocol, the server (domain name) and the path to the file: it specifies **where** the resource is located. It says nothing about the user. The protocol part (`http`) states how to reach it, but the main purpose of a URL is the location. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The access rule of the resource
The identity of the user of the resource

questions.enonce_markdown: System evaluation and feedback are key features of what phase of the SDLC?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the new system is in use, it is reviewed against the original objectives, the users' feedback is collected and corrections or improvements are made: this is the **maintenance (evaluation and review)** phase. Analysis and design come before the system exists, and implementation is the installation and changeover. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The IF- THEN is an example of a/an
questions.corrige_markdown: `IF ... THEN` chooses whether or not to execute a statement according to a condition: it is a **selection** (decision) statement. Repetition and iteration are the same thing (loops), and a sequence is a list of statements executed in order. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: How many DVDs of size 8GB capacity can be used to backup an 8 terabyte external hard disk?
questions.corrige_markdown: $1\ \mathrm{TB} = 1000\ \mathrm{GB}$ (or $1024\ \mathrm{GB}$ in binary units), so $8\ \mathrm{TB} = 8000\ \mathrm{GB}$ and the number of DVDs is $\dfrac{8000}{8} = 1000$ (with binary units $\dfrac{8 \times 1024}{8} = 1024$, which is also about one thousand). The other options are far too large. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is NOT commonly associated with online learning?

*Options as printed:* A) Lecture notes   B) White board   C) Calendar   D) E-mail
questions.corrige_markdown:
Online learning platforms deliver lecture notes, use e-mail for contact between teacher and students and often provide a virtual white board for live lessons. The **calendar** is a general organiser tool that is the least specific to online learning. The printed options are weak, since many platforms include a calendar and a white board is also a classroom object, so the key is a best guess by elimination.

**Intended answer: C (Calendar).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following programming languages is NOT machine independent?
questions.corrige_markdown: A machine-independent (portable) language can be compiled or interpreted on different types of computer. C, Pascal and Java are high-level languages with that property. **Assembly language** is a low-level language whose instructions map to the instruction set of one particular processor, so it is machine dependent. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A type of virus that replicates itself within a system overload the system resources is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **worm** copies itself repeatedly, inside a system and across a network, and consumes memory, processing time and bandwidth until the system slows down or crashes. A trojan pretends to be a useful program but does not replicate itself, adware displays advertisements and spyware secretly collects information. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a mobile operating system?
questions.corrige_markdown: iOS (Apple), Android (Google) and Windows (Windows Phone / Windows Mobile) are operating systems for phones and tablets. **Opera Mini** is a web browser, an application that runs on top of a mobile operating system. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: From the Gantt chart, one cannot easily identify:
questions.corrige_markdown: A Gantt chart is a bar chart with time on the horizontal axis: it shows when each task starts and ends and, by the overlapping bars, which tasks run at the same time. What it does **not** show clearly is the dependency between tasks (which task must finish before another can start); that is the strength of the PERT chart and of the critical path. The chart does not give costs either, but the wording "cannot easily identify" points to the dependencies, which can only be added as arrows. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: When tasks are to begin and end
Which tasks are dependent on others
The cost of executing each tasks

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following can be used to validate a designed algorithm?
questions.corrige_markdown: To validate an algorithm, it is traced by hand (or run) with **test data** chosen to cover normal, extreme and erroneous cases and the results are compared with the expected ones. Output, processes and constants are parts of an algorithm, not a way of checking it. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A software licence that makes the source code available to anyone who wants to modify is:
questions.corrige_markdown: **Open source** software is distributed with its source code, which anyone may read, modify and redistribute. Freeware is free to use but the source code is generally kept closed, shareware is used free for a limited time and a trial version is limited in time or features. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a risk associated with cloud computing?
questions.corrige_markdown: Automatic updates, mobility (access from anywhere) and scalability are benefits of cloud computing. Because the data is stored on the provider's servers and reached over the Internet, the risk is that it may be **exposed** to unauthorised access, breaches or loss of control. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Data is represented in CD-ROMs by
questions.corrige_markdown: On a CD-ROM the data is stored in a spiral track of tiny **pits** (hollows) and **lands** (flat areas); the laser reflects differently from each and the change is read as a binary value. "0's and 1's" is the logical content of the data, not the physical representation on the disk. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a limitation of E-commerce?
questions.corrige_markdown: Cheap prices, a small staff and no need for large premises are advantages of e-commerce. The need to buy, install and maintain **specialised software** (website, payment and stock systems) is a cost and a limitation. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Products can be sold at cheap prices
It needs a small number of staff
It does not need huge office space

questions.enonce_markdown: The principle of the Data Protection Act (1998) is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Among the eight principles of the Data Protection Act 1998, personal data must be accurate and, where necessary, **kept up to date**. There is no principle requiring immediate processing or that data be valuable, and "not stolen" is not worded as one of the principles (the Act requires appropriate security). **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Data should be kept up to date

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following is NOT a basic requirement to set up online communication?

*Options as printed:* A) A computer   B) A modem   C) A telephone   D) A web camera
questions.corrige_markdown:
Online communication needs a computer (or a similar device), a connection to the network (a modem or router and an Internet service provider) and communication software. A **web camera** is needed only for video communication: text, e-mail and voice chat work without one, so it is not a basic requirement. The telephone could also be defended, since a separate handset is not required either, which makes the printed question ambiguous.

**Intended answer: D (A web camera).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Arrange in order from fastest to slowest access time:
questions.corrige_markdown: The memory hierarchy, from fastest to slowest access, is: registers (inside the CPU), cache, main memory (RAM), and then secondary storage such as magnetic tape (sequential access, the slowest). Only option B follows that order. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A device that links several devices to a common channel:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **switch** has many ports and connects several devices of a local network to one common medium, forwarding each frame only to the port of its destination. A bridge joins two network segments, a router joins different networks and an access point links wireless devices to a wired network (it could also be argued here, but a switch is the usual device that links several wired devices together). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When part of a table depends on a field in the table that is not the table's primary key, it is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A **transitive dependency** occurs when a non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute rather than directly on the primary key (key $\to$ A $\to$ B); it must be removed to reach third normal form. A partial dependency is on **part of a composite** primary key (second normal form), and a foreign key is a field that links to another table. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which one of the following filing systems is commonly associated with 64 bits operating system?

*Options as printed:* A) eFAT   B) NTFS   C) FAT64   D) FAT32
questions.corrige_markdown:
FAT32 is the older 32-bit file system and has size limits. **NTFS** is the standard file system of 64-bit Windows, with 64-bit addressing, large files and volumes, security and journaling. "FAT64" is not a standard file system and exFAT (which "eFAT" probably means) is mainly used for removable media, so NTFS is the best choice, but the printed option A is unclear.

**Intended answer: B (NTFS).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A utility that optimises the hard disk by putting some file content in a contiguous area is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Files saved and deleted over time end up in scattered fragments. A **disk defragmenter** moves the pieces of each file together into a contiguous area so that the read head moves less and access is faster. Disk clean-up deletes unwanted files and compression reduces the size of files. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An application used by programmers to create source code, debug a code and manage the program is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: An **Integrated Development Environment (IDE)** combines a code editor, a compiler or interpreter, a debugger and project management tools in one application. A compiler, an interpreter or an editor does only one of those jobs. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT an Internet connection option for mobile devices?
questions.corrige_markdown: 4G (cellular data), Wi-Fi and WiMAX (printed "Winmax") are ways of connecting a mobile device to the Internet. **Android** is an operating system, not a connection technology. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The use of online tutorial lessons to prepare for examinations is known as
questions.corrige_markdown: Learning through lessons and tutorials delivered over the Internet is **e-learning**. Computer aided learning uses a computer program in the classroom or offline, distance learning is about the teacher and the learner being in different places (by post, radio or online), and "electronic studies" is not a standard term. **Answer: A.**
